ei.title: Tips and Tricks for a Healthier Digital Life

fullPassage:
Tips and Tricks for a Healthier Digital Life

Managing our digital lives can be challenging. Do you sometimes worry that your online content might face copyright issues? Have you ever felt that you were being overly influenced by online shopping recommendations? Are you constantly checking for likes and comments on your social media posts? If you answered yes to any of these questions, here are some tips and ideas to help you have a healthier digital life.

Avoid Copyright Violations
Cathy is an enthusiastic gamer who shares her gameplays on a popular video-sharing platform. Recently, her channel was suspended for copyright violation issues. She was shocked to learn that the background music played within the game had a copyright claim. Now Cathy wants to know how to avoid similar issues in the future.

Cathy's mistake is not uncommon in the content creation community. Creators often miss embedded copyrighted material, such as background music, sound effects, images, and video clips. Even a brief appearance of such material can put creators at risk of a copyright claim.

To avoid any potential copyright issues, creators should research their creation to check if any of its components are copyrighted. If they come across copyrighted content, they should contact the copyright owner for permission to use it, replace it with non-copyrighted material, or remove it completely. Utilizing material with a Creative Commons (CC) license might also be a good idea. Most of this material can be used at no cost as long as certain rules are followed. These simple steps can help content creators avoid unexpected copyright issues and have some peace of mind about their work.

Break Free from Filter Bubbles
Meet Alex, a high school student with a passion for fashion. He often finds inspiration on social media and enjoys shopping online. Recently, however, he has realized that he keeps buying the same style of clothes. Even when he wants to try out new styles, he has a difficult time getting fresh ideas or recommendations on his preferred online platforms.

Alex is trapped in a filter bubble! Online shops and social media platforms use algorithms to "filter" out content for you based on your past purchases, likes, and search history. As a result, you might find yourself stuck inside a "bubble" of limited information that only reinforces your existing beliefs and preferences. If Alex had been aware of this, he wouldn't have missed out on new and diverse styles outside his bubble.

To stay away from filter bubbles, it is important to regularly check whether you are already trapped inside one. One way to do this is by performing searches on your favorite online platforms after logging out. Compare the search results and recommendations with what you usually see when you are logged in. If there is a big difference between them, you may have been trapped in a filter bubble.

Managing your personal information is another key to avoiding filter bubbles. Whenever you go online, your activities are saved as cookies on your computer. Websites can collect them based on your consent. You can remove or limit your consent on the websites or delete the cookies on your computer on a regular basis. This way, you can reduce the amount of personal data that you unconsciously share as you visit websites. Take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas.

Be Happy on Social Media
Social media is a big part of Min's life. She posts photos every day and enjoys getting likes and comments. Lately, however, she began to be concerned about her social media activity. She realizes that she spends a considerable amount of time repeatedly checking her feed, desperately seeking more likes. She even feels disappointed when she sees her friends' posts receiving more likes than hers.

Social media is a powerful tool that helps us connect with others, but it also has its downsides. One of them is that many people place excessive value on the number of likes and comments they get on their posts. Those who feel that they don't get enough likes, like Min, may experience feelings of shame or rejection. This can lead to severe anxiety. In addition, comparing their posts with more popular ones can make them feel inferior and harm their self-esteem. It can even cause depression.

To make social media a positive part of your daily life, it is important to use it mindfully with some guidelines. First, don't let social media consume all your time and attention. A quick and easy way to do this is to set limits on your usage or take regular breaks from social media. This will free up your time and energy to engage in activities outside the online world. Second, keep in mind that social media is a tool to network with others, not a platform for competition. When you start to feel unpopular or inferior, remember that what you see online presents only the highlights of other people's lives and does not reflect their entire story. If you still feel envious, use that emotion as motivation that helps you with your personal growth. By following these rules, you can make the most of social media and feel more at ease in your digital interactions.

questions.passage: Cathy is an enthusiastic gamer who shares her gameplays on a popular video-sharing platform. Recently, her channel was ①<u>suspended</u> for copyright violation issues. She was shocked ②<u>learning</u> that the background music played within the game had a copyright claim. Now Cathy wants to know how ③<u>to avoid</u> similar issues ④<u>in</u> the future.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'to learn'인데 'learning'으로 바뀌었다. be shocked to V(~하고 충격받다) 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① suspended: 수동태 (was suspended = 정지되었다)
❌ ② learning → to learn: be shocked to V (감정 원인의 to부정사)
✅ ③ to avoid: how to V (의문사 + to부정사)
✅ ④ in: in the future (미래에)
det.tip: be shocked to V: ~하고 충격받다. 감정형용사 + to부정사(원인). be shocked learning (X).

questions.passage: Online shops and social media platforms use algorithms to ①<u>"filter"</u> out content for you based on your past purchases, likes, and search history. As a result, you might find yourself ②<u>stuck</u> inside a "bubble" of limited information that only ③<u>reinforces</u> your existing beliefs and preferences. If Alex had been aware of this, he ④<u>wouldn't miss</u> out on new and diverse styles outside his bubble.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'wouldn't have missed'인데 'wouldn't miss'로 바뀌었다. 가정법 과거완료(had been → wouldn't have p.p.) 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① "filter": 동사원형 (to filter out)
✅ ② stuck: find + 목적어 + 과거분사 (자신이 갇힌 것을 발견하다)
✅ ③ reinforces: 주격 관계대명사 that절 동사 (information that reinforces)
❌ ④ wouldn't miss → wouldn't have missed: If S had p.p., S would have p.p. (가정법 과거완료)
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: If had p.p. → would have p.p. 조건절 had been aware → 주절 wouldn't have missed.

questions.passage: Whenever you go online, your activities are saved as cookies on your computer. Websites can collect them based on your consent. You can remove or limit your consent on the websites or delete the cookies on your computer on a regular basis. This way, you can reduce the amount of personal data ①<u>what</u> you unconsciously share as you visit websites. Take action to break free from your filter bubble and open ②<u>yourself</u> up to new ideas ③<u>that</u> may surprise ④<u>you</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① 'personal data'라는 선행사가 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 필요하다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 쓸 수 없다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① what → that: 선행사 personal data가 있으므로 what 불가. that(목적격 관계대명사) 필요.
✅ ② yourself: 재귀대명사 (open yourself up)
✅ ③ that: 주격 관계대명사 (ideas that may surprise)
✅ ④ you: 목적격 대명사 (surprise you)
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that. 선행사가 있으면 that/which 사용. data what (X), data that (O).

questions.passage: Those who feel that they don't get enough likes, like Min, may experience feelings of shame or rejection. This can lead to severe anxiety. In addition, ①<u>comparing</u> their posts with more popular ones can make them feel ②<u>inferior</u> and harm their self-esteem. It can even cause ③<u>depression</u>. To make social media a positive part of your daily life, it is important ④<u>using</u> it mindfully with some guidelines.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'to use'인데 'using'으로 바뀌었다. It is important to V(~하는 것이 중요하다) 가주어-진주어 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① comparing: 동명사 주어 (comparing ~ can make)
✅ ② inferior: 형용사 보어 (feel inferior)
✅ ③ depression: 명사 (cause depression = 우울증을 야기하다)
❌ ④ using → to use: It is important to V (가주어 it, 진주어 to V)
det.tip: It is important to V: ~하는 것이 중요하다. It is important using (X). 가주어 구문은 to부정사.

questions.passage: Cathy's mistake is not ①<u>uncommon</u> in the content creation community. Creators often miss embedded copyrighted material, such as background music, sound effects, images, and video clips. Even a ②<u>brief</u> appearance of such material can put creators at risk of a copyright claim. To avoid any ③<u>potential</u> copyright issues, creators should research their creation to check if any of its components are copyrighted. Utilizing material with a Creative Commons (CC) license might also be a good idea. Most of this material can be used at no cost as long as certain rules are ④<u>violated</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'followed(준수되는)'인데 'violated(위반되는)'로 바뀌었다. CC 자료는 규칙을 따르면 무료로 쓸 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① uncommon(드문 일이 아닌): 원문 일치 (not uncommon = 흔한)
✅ ② brief(짧은): 원문 일치
✅ ③ potential(잠재적인): 원문 일치
❌ ④ violated(위반되는) → followed(준수되는): 규칙을 '따르면' 무료 사용 가능
det.tip: followed(따르다) ↔ violated(위반하다). as long as rules are followed = 규칙을 따르는 한.

questions.passage: Social media is a powerful tool that helps us connect with others, but it also has its downsides. One of them is that many people place ①<u>excessive</u> value on the number of likes and comments they get on their posts. Those who feel that they don't get enough likes may experience feelings of shame or ②<u>rejection</u>. In addition, comparing their posts with more popular ones can make them feel ③<u>superior</u> and harm their self-esteem. It can even cause ④<u>depression</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'inferior(열등한)'인데 'superior(우월한)'로 바뀌었다. 더 인기 있는 게시물과 비교하면 열등감을 느낀다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① excessive(과도한): 원문 일치
✅ ② rejection(거부감): 원문 일치
❌ ③ superior(우월한) → inferior(열등한): 인기 게시물과 비교 → 열등감
✅ ④ depression(우울증): 원문 일치
det.tip: inferior(열등한) ↔ superior(우월한). 더 인기 있는 것과 비교 → feel inferior.

questions.passage: Cathy is an enthusiastic gamer who shares her gameplays on a popular video-sharing platform. Recently, her channel was suspended for copyright violation issues. She was shocked to learn that the background music played within the game had a copyright claim. Now Cathy wants to know how to avoid similar issues in the future.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"Cathy의 채널은 그녀가 직접 작곡한 음악 때문에 정지되었다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 게임 내 배경 음악(background music played within the game)에 저작권 클레임이 있었다. Cathy가 직접 작곡한 음악이 아니다.
det.analysis: 채널 정지 원인 = 게임 속 배경 음악의 저작권 문제. '직접 작곡한 음악'은 거짓.
det.tip: background music played within the game ≠ 직접 작곡한 음악. 내장된 저작권 소재.

questions.passage: Online shops and social media platforms use algorithms to "filter" out content for you based on your past purchases, likes, and search history. As a result, you might find yourself stuck inside a "bubble" of limited information that only reinforces your existing beliefs and preferences. If Alex had been aware of this, he wouldn't have missed out on new and diverse styles outside his bubble.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"필터 버블은 사용자의 기존 신념과 선호를 강화하는 제한된 정보의 거품이다."

det.korean: T. 원문: 'a "bubble" of limited information that only reinforces your existing beliefs and preferences.' 정확히 일치.
det.analysis: 진술문과 원문의 필터 버블 정의가 완전히 일치한다.
det.tip: reinforces existing beliefs and preferences = 기존 신념과 선호를 강화. 정의 그대로.

questions.passage: Whenever you go online, your activities are saved as cookies on your computer. Websites can collect them based on your consent. You can remove or limit your consent on the websites or delete the cookies on your computer on a regular basis. This way, you can reduce the amount of personal data that you unconsciously share as you visit websites.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"웹사이트는 사용자의 동의 없이 자유롭게 쿠키를 수집할 수 있다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 'Websites can collect them based on your consent.' 동의에 기반하여 수집하므로, '동의 없이 자유롭게'는 거짓.
det.analysis: based on your consent = 동의에 기반하여. '동의 없이 자유롭게'는 정반대.
det.tip: consent = 동의. based on your consent = 동의에 근거하여.

questions.passage: Cathy's mistake is not uncommon in the content creation community. Creators often miss embedded copyrighted material, such as background music, sound effects, images, and video clips. Even a brief appearance of such material can put creators at risk of a copyright claim. To avoid any potential copyright issues, creators should __________ their creation to check if any of its components are copyrighted.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 저작권 문제를 피하려면 자신의 창작물을 조사(research)해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① research: 원문 일치. 구성 요소가 저작권이 있는지 확인하기 위해 조사
❌ ② publish(출판하다): 출판이 아니라 사전 확인이 필요
❌ ③ delete(삭제하다): 전체 삭제가 아니라 확인 후 조치
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 무시하면 저작권 문제 발생
det.tip: research = 조사하다. 저작권 문제 회피의 첫 단계는 조사.

questions.passage: To make social media a positive part of your daily life, it is important to use it mindfully with some guidelines. First, don't let social media consume all your time and attention. Second, keep in mind that social media is a tool to network with others, not a platform for competition. When you start to feel unpopular or inferior, remember that what you see online presents only the __________ of other people's lives and does not reflect their entire story.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 온라인에서 보이는 것은 다른 사람 삶의 하이라이트(highlights)일 뿐이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ highlights: 원문 일치. 삶의 좋은 부분만 보여준다는 의미
❌ ① struggles(고군분투): 문맥상 반대
❌ ② failures(실패): 문맥상 반대
❌ ④ routines(일상): 핵심 대비가 안 됨 (highlights vs entire story)
det.tip: highlights = 하이라이트, 가장 좋은 부분. entire story(전체 이야기)와 대비.

questions.passage: To avoid any potential copyright issues, creators should research their creation to check if any of its components are copyrighted. If they come across copyrighted content, they should contact the copyright owner for permission to use it, replace it with non-copyrighted material, or remove it completely. Utilizing material with a Creative Commons (CC) license might also be a good idea. Most of this material can be used at no cost as long as certain rules are followed.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 저작권이 있는 콘텐츠를 발견하면 반드시 삭제해야만 한다.
CC 라이선스 자료는 특정 규칙을 따르면 대부분 무료로 사용할 수 있다.
저작권 소유자에게 연락하는 것은 불법 행위이다.
모든 배경 음악은 CC 라이선스로 자유롭게 사용 가능하다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 'Most of this material can be used at no cost as long as certain rules are followed.' 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② CC 라이선스 자료 무료 사용: 원문 일치
❌ ① 삭제만이 아니라 허락 받기, 대체, 삭제 3가지 방법 제시
❌ ③ 저작권 소유자에게 연락은 합법적 조치
❌ ④ '모든 배경 음악'이 아니라 CC 라이선스 자료만 해당
det.tip: at no cost = 무료로. as long as = ~하는 한. CC 라이선스 = Creative Commons.

questions.passage: To stay away from filter bubbles, it is important to regularly check whether you are already trapped inside one. One way to do this is by performing searches on your favorite online platforms after logging out. Compare the search results and recommendations with what you usually see when you are logged in. If there is a big difference between them, you may have been trapped in a filter bubble.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 로그인 상태에서 검색해야 필터 버블 여부를 확인할 수 있다.
즐겨 쓰는 온라인 플랫폼에서 로그아웃 후 검색을 해 볼 수 있다.
로그인과 로그아웃 상태의 검색 결과를 비교해야 한다.
두 검색 결과에 큰 차이가 있으면 필터 버블에 갇혀 있을 수 있다.

det.korean: ① 원문: '로그아웃(logging out) 후' 검색하라고 했지, 로그인 상태에서만 확인하라고 하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 로그인 상태에서만 → 원문은 '로그아웃 후' 검색하여 비교하라는 것. 로그인만으로는 부족
✅ ② after logging out: 원문 일치
✅ ③ Compare the search results: 원문 일치
✅ ④ big difference → may have been trapped: 원문 일치
det.tip: 핵심: 로그아웃 후 검색 → 로그인 때와 비교. '로그인 상태에서만'은 불일치.

questions.passage: (a) Managing our digital lives can be challenging. (b) Do you sometimes worry that your online content might face copyright issues? (c) Have you ever felt that you were being overly influenced by online shopping recommendations? (d) If you answered yes to any of these questions, here are some tips and ideas helping you have a healthier digital life.
questions.stem: 위 (a)~(d) 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?

det.korean: (d) 원문은 'to help you have'인데 'helping you have'로 바뀌었다. tips and ideas to help = ~하는 데 도움이 되는(목적/형용사적 용법).
det.analysis:
✅ (a) Managing: 동명사 주어 정상
✅ (b) might face: 조동사 + 동사원형 정상
✅ (c) were being influenced: 과거진행수동 정상
❌ (d) helping → to help: tips and ideas to help (형용사적 to부정사로 명사 수식)
det.tip: 명사 + to V (형용사적 용법): ideas to help (O). ideas helping (X, 어색한 분사 수식).

questions.passage: Alex is trapped in a filter bubble! Online shops and social media platforms use algorithms to "filter" out content for you based on your past purchases, likes, and search history. As a result, you might find yourself stuck inside a "bubble" of limited information that only reinforces your existing beliefs and preferences.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"온라인 상점과 소셜 미디어 플랫폼은 당신의 과거 구매, 좋아요, 검색 기록에 기반하여 콘텐츠를 '필터링'하기 위해 (          )을/를 사용한다."

det.korean: 원문: 'use algorithms to "filter" out content'
det.analysis: algorithms = 알고리즘. 과거 구매/좋아요/검색 기록 기반으로 콘텐츠를 필터링하는 도구.
det.tip: algorithm = 알고리즘, 연산 규칙. SNS와 온라인 쇼핑몰의 추천 시스템 핵심.

questions.passage: If you still feel envious, use that emotion as motivation that helps you with your personal growth. By following these rules, you can make the most of social media and feel more at ease in your digital interactions.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"여전히 부러움을 느낀다면, 그 감정을 개인적 성장에 도움이 되는 (          )(으)로 활용하라."

det.korean: 원문: 'use that emotion as motivation that helps you with your personal growth'
det.analysis: motivation = 동기부여. 부러움이라는 감정을 성장의 동기로 전환하라는 조언.
det.tip: motivation = 동기, 동기부여. envious(부러운) → motivation(동기)으로 전환.

questions.passage: Social media is a powerful tool that helps us connect with others, but it also has its downsides. Those who feel that they don't get enough likes, like Min, may experience feelings of shame or rejection. This can lead to severe anxiety. In addition, comparing their posts with more popular ones can make them feel inferior and harm their self-esteem. One of the downsides is that many people __________.
questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ place / excessive / value / on / the / number / of / likes / and / comments ]
questions.wa: place excessive value on the number of likes and comments
accept: place excessive value on the number of likes and comments
Place excessive value on the number of likes and comments
place excessive value on the number of likes and comments.
Place excessive value on the number of likes and comments.

det.korean: 좋아요와 댓글의 수에 과도한 가치를 둔다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'place excessive value on the number of likes and comments.' 10단어 배열.
det.tip: place value on ~: ~에 가치를 두다. excessive value = 과도한 가치.

questions.passage: Alex is trapped in a filter bubble! Online shops and social media platforms use algorithms to "filter" out content for you based on your past purchases, likes, and search history. As a result, you might find yourself stuck inside a "bubble" of limited information that only reinforces your existing beliefs and preferences. To stay away from filter bubbles, it is important to regularly check whether you are already trapped inside one.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 개인정보 보호를 위한 법적 규제의 필요성
필터 버블의 원리와 이를 벗어나기 위한 방법

det.korean: 글의 주제: 필터 버블의 원리와 이를 벗어나기 위한 방법.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 필터 버블의 작동 원리(알고리즘 기반 필터링) + 확인/탈출 방법
❌ ① 경제적 이점 언급 없음
❌ ② 기술적 원리가 아니라 사용자 관점의 설명
❌ ③ 법적 규제 언급 없음
det.tip: filter bubble = 필터 버블. 알고리즘이 만드는 정보 편향의 거품.

questions.passage: To make social media a positive part of your daily life, it is important to use it mindfully with some guidelines. First, don't let social media consume all your time and attention. A quick and easy way to do this is to set limits on your usage or take regular breaks from social media. Second, keep in mind that social media is a tool to network with others, not a platform for competition. When you start to feel unpopular or inferior, remember that what you see online presents only the highlights of other people's lives and does not reflect their entire story. If you still feel envious, use that emotion as motivation that helps you with your personal growth. By following these rules, you can make the most of social media and feel more at ease in your digital interactions.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 소셜 미디어를 완전히 끊는 것이 정신 건강에 가장 좋다.
소셜 미디어를 의식적으로 사용하면 긍정적인 디지털 생활이 가능하다.
소셜 미디어의 좋아요 수가 자존감의 유일한 기준이다.
다른 사람의 게시물과 비교하는 것이 성장의 원동력이다.

det.korean: 요지: 소셜 미디어를 의식적으로(mindfully) 사용하면 긍정적인 디지털 생활이 가능하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 핵심: use it mindfully → make the most of social media + feel more at ease
❌ ① 완전히 끊으라는 것이 아니라 '의식적으로 사용'하라는 것
❌ ③ 좋아요 수에 과도한 가치를 두지 말라고 경고
❌ ④ 비교가 열등감을 유발한다고 경고, 원동력이라 하지 않음
det.tip: mindfully = 의식적으로. 핵심 메시지: 사용 시간 제한 + 경쟁 아닌 네트워킹.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"필터 버블에서 벗어나 새로운 아이디어에 마음을 열자."
[조건] take action / break free / open 을 사용할 것
questions.wa: Take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas.
accept: Take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas.
Take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas
take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas
take action to break free from your filter bubble and open yourself up to new ideas.

det.korean: 필터 버블에서 벗어나 새로운 아이디어에 마음을 열기 위해 행동에 나서자.
det.analysis: take action to V: ~하기 위해 행동하다. break free from: ~에서 벗어나다. open yourself up to: ~에 마음을 열다.
det.tip: break free from = ~에서 벗어나다. open up to = ~에 마음을 열다.
